questions.prompt: It is the custom for those to be praised who have bravely fallen in battle.
questions.answer: Mōs est laudārī eōs quī fortiter in proeliō cecidissent.

questions.prompt: I ask you to spare those whom you have conquered.
questions.answer: Tē rogō ut parcās eīs quōs vīceris.

questions.prompt: No danger was so great that the soldiers whom he led would flee.
questions.answer: Nūllum tantum perīculum erat ut mīlitēs quōs dūceret fugerent.

questions.prompt: When the scouts reported what they had seen, the leader rejoiced.
questions.answer: Cum explōrātōrēs nūntiārent quae vīdissent, dux gāvīsus est.

questions.prompt: The king ordered that the captives whom the soldiers had taken be freed.
questions.answer: Rēx iussit ut captīvī quōs mīlitēs cēpissent līberārentur.

questions.prompt: It is necessary for those to be feared who despise the laws.
questions.answer: Necesse est timērī eōs quī lēgēs contemnant.

questions.prompt: I fear that the man in whom you trust may deceive you.
questions.answer: Vereor nē vir cui crēdās tē dēcipiat.

questions.prompt: So great was his desire that he scorned whatever dangers stood in the way.
questions.answer: Tanta erat eius libīdō ut perīcula quae obstārent contemneret.

questions.prompt: Let no one hope for a reward which he has not earned.
questions.answer: Nēmō spēret praemium quod nōn meruerit.

questions.prompt: The custom was for the gods to be worshipped who protected the city.
questions.answer: Mōs erat colī deōs quī urbem tuērentur.

questions.prompt: So that the soldiers might keep what they had gained, he fortified the camp.
questions.answer: Ut mīlitēs retinērent quae adeptī essent, castra mūnīvit.

questions.prompt: No day passed on which he did not read something he loved.
questions.answer: Nūllus diēs praeteriit quō nōn aliquid quod amāret legeret.

questions.prompt: It is fitting for those to be blamed who neglect what they ought to do.
questions.answer: Decet reprehendī eōs quī neglegant quae facere dēbeant.

questions.prompt: It is fitting that those be praised who defend what they cherish.
questions.answer: Decet eōs laudārī quī dēfendant quod dīligant.

questions.prompt: When they brought forward differing reasons, while each expressed what he felt, the senate deliberated.
questions.answer: Cum dīversās causās afferrent, dum quisque exprimeret quod sentīret, senātus dēlīberābat.

questions.prompt: Should I be ashamed of that which I myself freely confess?
questions.answer: Num mē pudeat eius quod ipse fatear?

questions.prompt: Let no one drink what he has not himself prepared.
questions.answer: Nēmō pōtet quod ipse nōn parāverit.

questions.prompt: It befits a good citizen to burn with love for whatever is honorable.
questions.answer: Bonum cīvem decet ārdēre amōre eius quod honestum sit.

questions.prompt: When the guests consumed what had been set before them, the host rejoiced.
questions.answer: Cum convīvae cōnsūmerent quod appositum esset, hospes gaudēbat.

questions.prompt: I would praise the man who changed his opinion when reason demanded it.
questions.answer: Laudem eum quī sententiam immūtāret cum ratiō postulāret.

questions.prompt: It is the custom for those soldiers to be praised who have guarded the walls.
questions.answer: Mōs est eōs mīlitēs laudārī quī moenia custōdīverint.

questions.prompt: No one has been found so brave that he did not fear what he could not see.
questions.answer: Nēmō tam fortis inventus est quī nōn timēret quod vidēre nōn posset.

questions.prompt: Should I now fear that which I myself once dared with a bold heart?
questions.answer: Quod ipse ōlim animō audācī ausus sim, nunc timeam?

questions.prompt: The farmer hid the grain so that he might keep for winter whatever he had gathered.
questions.answer: Agricola frūmentum cēlāvit ut in hiemem servāret quidquid collēgisset.

questions.prompt: It is fitting for those to be rewarded who have preserved what their ancestors handed down.
questions.answer: Decet eōs praemiīs afficī quī servāverint quod māiōrēs trādiderint.

questions.prompt: Since each was pursuing what he himself desired, they could not agree.
questions.answer: Cum sequerentur quod quisque cuperet, cōnsentīre nōn poterant.

questions.prompt: No one is so wise that he scorns what he does not understand.
questions.answer: Nēmō tam sapiēns est ut contemnat quod nōn intellegat.

questions.prompt: May those perish who betray whatever they have sworn to defend.
questions.answer: Pereant quī prōdant quidquid dēfendere iūrāverint.

questions.prompt: It is shameful for a man to boast of that which he has not accomplished.
questions.answer: Turpe est hominem glōriārī dē eō quod nōn perfēcerit.

questions.prompt: Do not condemn a man for a crime which he has not committed.
questions.answer: Nē damnēs hominem ob scelus quod nōn commīserit.

questions.prompt: When the envoys had set forth what each city demanded, the senate hesitated.
questions.answer: Cum lēgātī exposuissent quod quaeque cīvitās postulāret, senātus dubitāvit.

questions.prompt: So great was the storm that the merchants threw away whatever they had bought.
questions.answer: Tanta tempestās fuit ut mercātōrēs abicerent quidquid ēmissent.

questions.prompt: He orders them, till the affair should be decided, to keep the man; when it is judged, to bring him to him.
questions.answer: Imperat, dum rēs iūdicētur, hominem adservent: cum iūdicāta sit, ad sē ut addūcant.

questions.prompt: For who is so reckless of spirit that, when he sees these things, he can keep silent and pass them by?
questions.answer: Etenim quis tam dissolūtō animō est, quī haec cum videat, tacēre ac neglegere possit?

questions.prompt: He orders the bridge which was near Geneva torn up.
questions.answer: pontem, quī erat ad Genāvam, iubet rescindī.

questions.prompt: I give up, because I have to.
questions.answer: concēdō, quia necesse est.

questions.prompt: I am afraid I may make the work harder, while I am aiming to make it less.
questions.answer: vereor nē, dum minuere velim labōrem, augeam.

questions.prompt: If you should pronounce only such people unhappy as had to die, you would not except one of those who were living.
questions.answer: sī sōlōs eōs dīcerēs miserōs, quibus moriendum esset, nēminem eōrum, quī vīverent exciperēs.

questions.prompt: It is the custom at Syracuse, that if any question is discussed in the senate, anybody who pleases may express his opinion.
questions.answer: mōs est Syrācūsīs, ut sī quā dē rē ad senātum referātur, dīcat sententiam quī velit.

questions.prompt: The sage does not hesitate, if this be the better course, to withdraw from life.
questions.answer: sapiēns nōn dubitat, sī ita melius sit, migrāre dē vītā.
